symptoms: Status epilepticus: continuous seizures for >= 5 minutes, or >= 2 discrete seizures in close succession without full recovery of consciousness between episodes.
Refractory status epilepticus: seizures persisting despite >= 2 anticonvulsant agents (1st and 2nd line).

management_steps.details: ABCD approach to initial resuscitation. Don't ever forget glucose — hypoglycaemia: 1ml/kg of 50% dextrose IV (or 5ml/kg 10% dextrose in children); if no IV line, 50% dextrose buccal (1ml in children, 2-5ml in adults). Lateral patient position, supplemental oxygen. Rapid sequence intubation if seizures continue >= 5 minutes.

Lorazepam 0.1mg/kg IV (max rate 2mg/min), OR Clonazepam 0.02mg/kg IV, OR Diazepam 0.2-0.3mg/kg IV (max rate 5mg/min), OR Midazolam 0.2mg/kg IV or 0.3mg/kg buccal/intranasal. If the seizure continues, give a second dose of the chosen benzodiazepine.

Phenytoin 20mg/kg IV (max rate 50mg/min), OR Sodium Valproate 20-30mg/kg IV (max rate 3-6mg/kg/min), OR Phenobarbitone 20mg/kg IV. If seizure continues after 20 minutes, repeat at half dose: Phenytoin 10mg/kg IV, Sodium Valproate 10mg/kg IV, or Phenobarbitone 10mg/kg.

Midazolam infusion: loading dose 0.2mg/kg IV then 0.1mg/kg/hr (range 0.05-2mg/kg/hr). Propofol infusion: loading dose 3-5mg/kg IV then 1-15mg/kg/hr. Ketamine infusion: loading dose 1.5mg/kg then 0.01-0.05mg/kg/hr.

Consider infection/intoxication, metabolic/electrolyte abnormalities, trauma/toxins, drug toxicity, eclampsia, intracranial haemorrhage/ischaemic stroke. ECG, blood glucose and blood gas on all patients; urine bHCG on all female patients. Urgent CT brain with contrast if no return to baseline or focal neurological deficit. Consult Neurology/ICU.

warnings: Always check blood glucose before/alongside anticonvulsant therapy — never forget the glucose.
